decisions.reason: As a training offer closely tied to the installed base and service capabilities, it likely meets modest aspiration levels and can be sustained with relatively little resource strain.

As an accessory that builds on the core machinery business, it fits existing customers and capabilities, so even if sales are uneven it is still worth keeping unless performance clearly falls below aspirations.

Because it is distant from the firm’s established offer and was only weakly signalled on the market, management would be more likely to judge it against aspiration shortfalls and reallocate resources to nearer opportunities.

A high-speed CNC milling machine line is very close to the firm’s core business, strategically important, and supported by its R&D, service, and modular engineering strengths, making withdrawal unlikely.
The automatic tool change system complements the firm’s existing machines and productivity promise, so its fit with established offerings and customer needs supports retention.
